server.name: Data Legion
server.title: Data Legion
server.description: Enrich and search US people and global companies; clean, hash and validate the inputs.

protocolMetadata.instructions: Data Legion provides enriched person and company data. Use person_enrich to look up people by email, phone, name, or social URL. Use person_search for SQL queries against the people database (use SELECT * FROM people WHERE ...). Use company_enrich to look up companies by domain, name, or ticker. Use company_search for SQL queries against the companies database (use SELECT * FROM companies WHERE ...). Use utility tools to clean, hash, or validate input data before enrichment. Use report_person / report_company to flag a data-quality issue with a record you looked up (e.g. a wrong or outdated field). The natural-language /person/discover and /company/discover endpoints are not exposed via MCP today; call them from the REST API or SDKs.

tool.name: person_enrich
tool.title: Enrich Person
tool.description:
Enrich a person by email, phone, name, social URL, or other identifiers.

Requires at least one primary identifier (email, phone, social_url, linkedin_id,
legion_id, email_hash) OR name + context (location, company, school, job_title, birth_date).

Returns detailed person profile including contact info, work experience,
education, skills, and more. Each successful match consumes one credit.
Field access is determined by the team's contract.

Returns JSON `{"matches": [{"person": {...}, "match_metadata": {...}}], "total": n}`:
the best match, its `match_metadata` (`matched_on`: the input fields that matched,
`match_type`, `match_confidence`: high, moderate or low), and `total`, the number of
matches found. No match is an error (HTTP 404) and costs nothing.

Key person fields: `legion_id`, `full_name`, `job_title`, `seniority_level`,
`job_function`, `company_name`, `company_domain`, `work_email`, `mobile_phone`,
`emails`, `phones`, `linkedin_url`, `city`, `state`, `country`, `experience`,
`education`, `skills`, `last_seen`. `emails` and `phones` are lists with
`address`/`number` and `type`.

city.title: City
city.description: City of the person's location, as matching context.

email.title: Email
email.description: The person's email address, personal or work. Normalized before matching.

phone.title: Phone
phone.description: The person's phone number, in any common format. Normalized to E.164.

state.title: State
state.description: State of the person's location: a name ('texas') or code ('TX').

school.title: School
school.description: A school the person attended, as matching context: a name, website or social URL.

address.title: Address
address.description: The person's full street address as one string; parsed into city, state, postal code and country.

company.title: Company
company.description: The person's employer, as matching context: a company name, website or social URL.

country.title: Country
country.description: Country of the person's location: a name or code.

full_name.title: Full Name
full_name.description: The person's full name, e.g. 'Jane Doe'. A name alone is not enough: pair it with location, company, school, job_title or birth_date.

job_title.title: Job Title
job_title.description: The person's job title, as matching context with a name.

last_name.title: Last Name
last_name.description: The person's last name, given with first_name instead of full_name.

legion_id.title: Legion Id
legion_id.description: Data Legion's ID for the person: the `legion_id` of an earlier person_enrich or person_search result. Matched exactly.

titlecase.title: Titlecase
titlecase.description: If true, lowercase text fields (names, job titles, company names, industries, locations, skills, headlines) come back in title case. IDs, URLs, codes, raw fields and confidence fields are unchanged.

birth_date.title: Birth Date
birth_date.description: The person's date of birth as YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM or YYYY.

email_hash.title: Email Hash
email_hash.description: SHA-256 (64 hex characters), SHA-1 (40) or MD5 (32) hash of the normalized email address, for lookups without the plain email. utility_hash_email makes one.

first_name.title: First Name
first_name.description: The person's first name, given with last_name instead of full_name.

social_url.title: Social Url
social_url.description: URL of the person's LinkedIn, X/Twitter, GitHub or Facebook profile; the network is detected from the URL.

linkedin_id.title: Linkedin Id
linkedin_id.description: The person's LinkedIn numeric ID (the `linkedin_id` field of a person result). For a LinkedIn profile URL, use social_url.

postal_code.title: Postal Code
postal_code.description: Postal or ZIP code of the person's location.

exclude_fields.title: Exclude Fields
exclude_fields.description: Comma-separated response fields to drop, applied after include_fields (e.g. 'skills,education'). Unknown field names are rejected with the valid list.

include_fields.title: Include Fields
include_fields.description: Comma-separated response fields to return; all other fields are dropped. Dot paths select a subfield (e.g. 'full_name,emails.address'). Omit to return every field. Unknown field names are rejected with the valid list.

min_confidence.title: Min Confidence
min_confidence.description: Drop matches below this match confidence: 'high', 'moderate' or 'low' (any other value is rejected). Omit for no minimum.

required_fields.title: Required Fields
required_fields.description: Comma-separated fields a match must have, or it is dropped: response field names ('work_email,phones'), a non-empty list subfield ('emails.type'), or a subfield equal to a value ('emails.type:personal', 'phones.type:mobile', 'socials.network:linkedin'). Unknown names or values return HTTP 400.

result.description: The API response as compact JSON text: {"matches": [{"<person|company>": {...}, "match_metadata": {"matched_on", "match_type", "match_confidence"}}], "total": <int>}: the best match and how many matches were found.

tool.name: person_search
tool.title: Search People
tool.description:
Search for people using SQL WHERE syntax.

Write a SELECT query against the 'people' table. The query must start with
SELECT. Do NOT include a LIMIT or OFFSET clause (the API rejects both); page
with the `limit` and `offset` parameters instead. Example:
  query: "SELECT * FROM people WHERE company_name ILIKE '%google%' AND state = 'california'"
  limit: 2
  offset: 0   # page 1; pass offset: 2 for page 2 with limit: 2

Available columns include: first_name, last_name, full_name, email, phone,
job_title, company_name, company_industry, city, state, state_code, country,
linkedin_url, and more. Text values are lowercase: `state` is the full name
('texas'), `state_code` the ISO code ('US-TX'), `country` the full name
('united states'). A title filter alone (`job_title ILIKE '%sales%'`) scans
everyone and can time out; pair it with a state, city or company filter.
Cross-table columns (title, organization_name, skills, headline, summary)
are automatically rewritten to subqueries.

Returns JSON `{"matches": [{"person": {...}}], "total": n}`: one page of person
records (the same fields as person_enrich) and `total`, the number of people the
WHERE clause matches across the database (an estimate for very broad queries).
Each person returned consumes one credit.

`include_fields` / `exclude_fields` take the same names as person_enrich. Full
profiles are large (up to ~10k tokens each), which is why `limit` defaults to 2,
like person_enrich; to list more people, name the fields you need in
include_fields and raise `limit`.

tool.name: company_enrich
tool.title: Enrich Company
tool.description:
Enrich a company by domain, name, LinkedIn, or ticker symbol.

Requires at least one identifier. The 'industry' field narrows name-based matching
but is not a standalone lookup. It must be a lowercase LinkedIn Industry V2
taxonomy value (e.g. 'software development') — a free-text value matches nothing
and silently zeroes the results. Returns company profile including employee counts,
workforce analytics, hiring/attrition trends, and distribution breakdowns.

Returns JSON `{"matches": [{"company": {...}, "match_metadata": {...}}], "total": n}`:
the best match, its `match_metadata` (`matched_on`, `match_type`,
`match_confidence`: high, moderate or low), and `total`, the number of matches
found. Each match consumes one credit; no match is an error (HTTP 404) and costs
nothing.

Key company fields: `legion_id`, `name` (object: `display`, `cleaned`, `raw`), `domain`,
`industry`, `size` (band), `founded`, `type`, `description`, `linkedin_url`,
`linkedin_employee_count` (the company's LinkedIn figure),
`legion_employee_count` (people Data Legion tracks at the company; a floor, not a
full headcount), `legion_new_hire_count`, `legion_attrition_count`,
`legion_employee_growth_rate`, `legion_employee_count_by_month`,
`legion_seniority_distribution`, `legion_job_function_distribution`, `tickers`,
`socials`, `domains`.

The hiring, attrition, growth and turnover windows (1m/3m/6m/12m) end at the
last month of `legion_employee_count_by_month`, not today. Job changes reach
profiles months after they happen, so the most recent months fill in over later
releases: read a low recent month as incomplete data, not a hiring freeze.

tool.name: utility_clean
tool.title: Clean Input Fields
tool.description:
Clean and normalize one or more data fields.

Pass a dict of field names to values. Supported person fields: email, phone,
full_name, first_name, last_name, state, country, social_url, school. Supported
company fields: company, domain, linkedin_company_url, ticker_symbol.

Returns JSON `{"results": {<field>: {"original", "cleaned", "normalized"}}}`: for
each field, the value sent, the cleaned value, and whether cleaning changed it.
`cleaned` is a string, except state and country (always `{full_name, code}`; an
unrecognized value comes back lowercased as `full_name`), social_url (`{url,
network}`), and company and school (`{name, type}`, `{domain, type}` or `{url,
network, type}`). Any other value it can't clean comes back as the trimmed input.
An unsupported field name or an empty value is an error. Free; no credits.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: The raw values to clean, each under the name of the field it holds, e.g. {"email": "John.Doe+tag@gmail.com", "phone": "(555) 123-4567"}. Use the field names the tool description lists.

default_region.title: Default Region
default_region.description: The country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, e.g. 'GB') whose numbering plan reads a phone number written without its country code. Only the phone field uses it.

result.title: Result
result.description: The API response as compact JSON text: {"results": {<field>: {"original", "cleaned", "normalized"}}}: one entry per field.

tool.name: utility_hash_email
tool.title: Hash Email Address
tool.description:
Hash an email address for privacy-preserving lookups.

Returns JSON `{"email", "normalized_email", "hashes": {"sha256", "sha1", "md5"}}`:
the email sent, the normalized form that was hashed, and its hex digests. Any of
the hashes can be used with person_enrich's email_hash parameter. Free; no credits.

email.title: Email
email.description: The plain email address to hash. Normalized before hashing; placeholder and role addresses (test@, info@, an example.com domain) are rejected.

result.title: Result
result.description: The API response as compact JSON text: {"email", "normalized_email", "hashes": {"sha256", "sha1", "md5"}}: hex digests.

tool.name: utility_validate
tool.title: Validate Input Fields
tool.description:
Validate person or company data and get cleaning suggestions.

Pass any combination of fields to validate. Use this before enrichment to ensure
data quality and improve match rates.

Returns JSON `{"valid", "errors", "warnings", "suggestions"}`: `valid` is false
when any field has an error; each error and warning names the `field`, the
`value`, the problem (`error` / `warning`) and an optional `suggestion`; each
suggestion gives a `field` and its `cleaned` value. Free; no credits.

phone.description: A phone number to check, in any format; one without a country code is read as US.

tool.name: report_person
tool.title: Report Person Data Issue
tool.description:
Report a data-quality issue with a person record (by legion_id).

Use this to flag bad/incorrect/outdated person data you got from
person_enrich or person_search so it can be reviewed and corrected. No credit
cost; available to any signed-in user or valid API key.

`field`: omit for 'record'; required for 'group' (a field-group slug) and
'field' (a response field name). At least one of `correct_value` or `comment`
is required.

Returns JSON confirming the recorded report: `report_id`, `status`, `subject_type`,
`legion_id`, `issue_type`, `issue_level`, `field` and `created_at`. Each call
records a new report.

field.title: Field
field.description: What the issue targets. Omit for 'record'; for 'group', a field group (e.g. 'experience', 'emails', 'locations'); for 'field', a response field name.

legion_id.title: Legion Id
legion_id.description: The `legion_id` of the person record being reported, from a person_enrich or person_search result.

issue_type.title: Issue Type
issue_type.description: What is wrong: 'incorrect' (a value is wrong), 'outdated' (a value is stale), 'misattributed' (a value belongs to someone else), 'frankenstein' (the record merges several real people), 'not_a_real_person' (no real individual behind it), or 'duplicate' (a duplicated value or record). Whole record: frankenstein, not_a_real_person; one group or field: incorrect, outdated, misattributed; any level: duplicate.

issue_level.title: Issue Level
issue_level.description: How much of the record is wrong: 'record' (all of it), 'group' (one field group, named in field) or 'field' (one response field, named in field).

correct_value.title: Correct Value
correct_value.description: The value that would be correct, if known.

observed_value.title: Observed Value
observed_value.description: The value the record currently holds that you dispute.

result.title: Result
result.description: The API response as compact JSON text: {"report_id", "status", "subject_type", "legion_id", "issue_type", "issue_level", "field", "created_at"}: the report as recorded.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Data Legion to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Data Legion to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://api.datalegion.ai/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is Data Legion MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 15, 2026, Data Legion scores 100/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is Data Legion's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 15, 2026, Data Legion scores 91/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 9 of 9 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Data Legion?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Data Legion in sales-and-marketing on the Manufact MCP catalog include Griddo AX Docs, Rocket Sloth, Affonso.io, Datacircle, and Tolt.
